accuracy.evidence: Placement checked against Letters and Sounds (DfES 2007) Phase One Aspect 7 'Oral blending and segmenting' (robot talk, sound-talk I spy, blending with body actions), Development Matters (DfE 2021) Literacy 3-4 'count or clap syllables in a word' and Reception 'blend sounds into words'. The big-to-small order (compound words, syllables, onset-rime, phonemes) follows Goswami and Bryant (1990) and Anthony and Lonigan (2004); the claim that phoneme blending supports early reading is the National Reading Panel (2000) finding. Every word is segmented by phoneme, not letter: f-i-sh is 3 sounds and d-u-ck ends in one /k/ sound, and the lab says so. Syllable splits (ba-na-na, rab-bit, el-e-phant) match spoken beats.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented oral-blending slips named in the adult text: sounds kept apart (releasing rain and bow with a gap is refused, 'apart' in the challenge, m4), choosing by the first part only (balloon and basket for ba-na-na, rainbow and robot for rab-bit, hat for c…at, pen for p…ig: 'first'), missing the middle sound (bed for b-a-g, cap for c-u-p, sock for s-u-n, m3: 'middle'), missing the last sound (cow for c…at, cap for c-a-t, bell for b-e-d: 'last'), wrong order (bus for s-u-n, n-u-s: 'order'), blending before every sound is heard (clapping early is refused, predict 4, p5: 'early'), counting beats wrongly (egg, bear: 'short'), and thinking letters or letter names are needed ('letters', 'names', m7).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagoralblend is a listening lab with no letters to decode: a slider-like drag that closes the gap between two spoken words until they touch, matching a word clapped in beats to its picture, giving Robot the toy it says in onset-rime and phoneme talk, tapping one sound onto head, tummy and toes before a clap that blends, and a six-object I spy room with a near miss each round. 414 Blending sounds to read words (flagblend) reads printed graphemes with a blending car, 361 Onsets and rimes (flagrime) swaps written onsets, and 201 Syllables counts beats without blending them back; none works by ear alone. Shingle similarity to every flag_*.js is under 30% (gate passes).

lab_teaches.evidence: The child discovers each idea by acting: rain and bow stay two words until the second card is pushed right up close (a part-way drop is refused with 'still a gap'), the picture panel only fills when the parts touch; wrong pictures that share the first beat or sound are refused with the part that differs; the head, tummy, toes scene refuses toes-first and refuses a clap before the third sound, then shows dog and fish with 'fish has 4 letters but only 3 sounds'; I spy keeps a near miss (bed next to bag, cap next to cup) on screen every round. Done messages confirm only after the action.

predictions.evidence: Three predictions, each with a tempting wrong option the lab then disproves: 'still two things: rain and a bow' (pushing them together makes rainbow), 'Yes, it ends the same' for hat after c…at (the hat card is refused: listen to the first sound), and 'Yes: duck!' after only d (the clap is refused until all three sounds are tapped, and the word is dog).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Seven rotating challenge questions whose wrong answers carry eight distinct slip messages built from the sounds Robot said: last ('cap ends a different way. Robot said c-a-t'), first, middle ('bag has a different middle'), short ('bear has fewer beats'), apart, early ('d … could be lots of words, like dog or duck'), order ('same sounds, wrong order. Robot said n-u-s') and letters or letter names ('c-a-t, not see-ay-tee'). Checked on a phone screenshot: the cap answer shows the last-sound message.

readability.evidence: Kid text is four short paragraphs of one-syllable words (bits, push, beats, sound, end) passing the learner limit in validate_lessons.py; lab text is two to eight words per card with a picture on every choice, made for a grown-up to read aloud to a 3 to 4 year old. Adult text passes the adult limit while keeping the precise terms (oral blending, syllable, onset and rime, phoneme, phonological awareness, letter names versus sounds).

no_filler.evidence: Each kid paragraph teaches one step (two words, beats, single sounds, listen to the end). Adult paragraphs give the curriculum placement, the big-to-small order with its research, the named mistakes with how to say sounds, and what the lab does. No content-gate filler matches; the lab text is only instructions, the sounds Robot says and feedback.

mobile.evidence: Checked on 360 px Android screenshots in light and dark for every step before and after Show me: the Robot bubble fits up to three sound beads, the two word cards and the 3-word result panel fit side by side, three picture cards fit across with 34 px pictures, the head/tummy/toes column and Clap button sit in two columns without clipping, and the six-object I spy grid is 3 by 2 with readable labels. The canvas is 1.3 times as tall as wide on phones; walk.cjs passed on iPhone 13 and desktop. The drop box shows open hands, not a basket, so it is not confused with the basket picture.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a labelled button twin: Push closer, Give Robot the <word>, Tap head / tummy / toes, Clap, and one button per I spy object; cards can also be tapped to pick and then the drop box tapped. The canvas aria-label is rewritten with each scene description and each piece of feedback, challenge feedback is a role=status live region, right and wrong tiles carry ✓ / ✗ text as well as colour, and axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) found nothing in light or dark on desktop and phone.
